# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

      if (targetEntity instanceof Wall || targetEntity instanceof Player) {

      return new Success();

  public void move(final Position from, final Position to)
  {
    if (Math.abs(from.getX() - to.getX()) + Math.abs(from.getY() - to.getY()) != 1) {
      return;
    }

    Entity fromEntity = getEntity(from);
    if (!(fromEntity instanceof Player)) {
      return;
    }
    Player player = (Player) fromEntity;
    int playerId = player.getId();

    Entity toEntity = getEntity(to);

    if (toEntity instanceof Wall || toEntity instanceof Player) {
      return;
    }
    if (toEntity instanceof Box && !((Box) toEntity).isPushable()) {
      return;
    }

    if (toEntity == null || toEntity instanceof Empty) {
      getEntities().remove(from);
      getEntities().put(to, player);
      getCurrentTransition().recordMove(from, to);
    } else if (toEntity instanceof Box) {
      Box box = (Box) toEntity;
      if (box.getOwnerId() != playerId) {
        return;
      }
      int dx = to.getX() - from.getX();
      int dy = to.getY() - from.getY();
      Position behind = new Position(to.getX() + dx, to.getY() + dy);
      Entity behindEntity = getEntity(behind);
      if (behindEntity != null && !(behindEntity instanceof Empty)) {
        return;

      getEntities().remove(from);
      getEntities().remove(to);
      getEntities().put(to, player);
      getEntities().put(behind, box);
      getCurrentTransition().recordMove(from, to);
      getCurrentTransition().recordMove(to, behind);
      checkpoint();
    }

   *       iii. If state.getEntity(behindPos) is not Empty, return new Failed("Cannot push box, space behind is occupied")
   *    f. Execute move: state.move(currentPos, nextPos)
   *    g. If a Box was pushed, invoke state.checkpoint()
   *    h. Return new Success()
   * 2. Else if action is an instance of Undo:
   *    a. If state.getUndoQuota() == 0, return new Failed("Undo quota exhausted")
   *    b. If state.history is not empty:
   *       i. Invoke state.undo()
   *       ii. If state.getUndoQuota() > 0, decrement state.undoQuota by 1
   *    c. Return new Success()
   * 3. Else if action is an instance of Exit:
   *    a. Set isExitSpecified = true
   *    b. Return new Success()
   * 4. Else (e.g., InvalidInput):
   *    a. Return new Failed("Invalid input command")
   * Related Features: state, isExitSpecified, ActionResult, GameStateTransition, TransitionStack
   * Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, Box, Empty, Exit, Failed, GameState, InvalidInput, Move, Player, Position, Success, Undo, Wall
   * Input: action : Action (Contains initiator int ID, type discriminator, and directional/target data)
   * Output: ActionResult (Either Success or Failed containing a reason String)
   * Pre-condition: state is fully initialized and reflects a valid board configuration; action is not null; if Move, initiator corresponds to a valid player currently on the board; if Undo, undoQuota permits execution.
   * Post-condition: Internal GameState is updated according to action semantics; isExitSpecified is set to true if Exit triggered; appropriate ActionResult is returned reflecting outcome and reason; undoQuota is decremented if a checkpoint was successfully undone.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public ActionResult processAction(final Action action)
  {
    if (action instanceof Move) {
      Move moveAction = (Move) action;
      Position currentPos = state.getPlayerPositionById(action.initiator);
      Position nextPos = moveAction.nextPosition(currentPos);
      Object targetEntity = state.getEntity(nextPos);
      
      if (targetEntity instanceof Wall || targetEntity instanceof Player) {
        return new Failed("Movement blocked or invalid target");
      }
      
      if (targetEntity instanceof Box) {
        Box box = (Box) targetEntity;
        if (box.getPlayerId() != action.initiator) {
          return new Failed("Cannot push another player's box");
        }
        
        Position behindPos = moveAction.nextPosition(nextPos);
        Object behindEntity = state.getEntity(behindPos);
        if (!(behindEntity instanceof Empty)) {
          return new Failed("Cannot push box, space behind is occupied");
        }
      }
      
      state.move(currentPos, nextPos);
      if (targetEntity instanceof Box) {
        state.checkpoint();
      }
      return new Success();
    } else if (action instanceof Undo) {
      if (state.getUndoQuota() == 0) {
        return new Failed("Undo quota exhausted");
      }
      if (!state.getHistory().isEmpty()) {
        state.undo();
        if (state.getUndoQuota() > 0) {
          state.setUndoQuota(state.getUndoQuota() - 1);
        }
      }
      return new Success();
    } else if (action instanceof Exit) {
      setIsExitSpecified(true);
      return new Success();
    } else {
      return new Failed("Invalid input command");
    }
  }

      return;

      return;

      getEntities().put(behind, box);

  public GameMap parseGameMap(final String mapText)
  {
    
        if (mapText == null)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map file.");
        }
    
        final List<String> lines = java.util.Arrays.asList(mapText.split("\\R"));
        if (lines.isEmpty() || lines.get(0).trim().isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map file.");
        }
    
        final int undoLimit;
        try
        {
          undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines.get(0).trim());
        }
        catch (NumberFormatException e)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("Failed to parse undo limit.", e);
        }
    
        if (undoLimit < -1)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("invalid undo limit");
        }
    
        final List<String> mapLines = lines.subList(1, lines.size());
        if (mapLines.isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map file.");
        }
    
        int maxHeight = mapLines.size();
        int maxWidth = 0;
        for (String line : mapLines)
        {
          if (line.length() > maxWidth)
          {
            maxWidth = line.length();
          }
        }
    
        final Map<Position, Entity> entityMap = new HashMap<Position, Entity>();
        final EList<Position> destinations = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Position>();
    
        final java.util.Set<Integer> players = new java.util.HashSet<>();
        final java.util.Set<Integer> referencedPlayers = new java.util.HashSet<>();
        int boxCount = 0;
    
        for (int y = 0; y < mapLines.size(); y++)
        {
          String line = mapLines.get(y);
          for (int x = 0; x < line.length(); x++)
          {
            char ch = line.charAt(x);
    
            Position position = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createPosition();
            position.setX(x);
            position.setY(y);
    
            switch (ch)
            {
              case '#':
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createWall());
                break;
              case '.':
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
                break;
              case '@':
                destinations.add(position);
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
                break;
              default:
                if (ch >= 'A' && ch <= 'Z')
                {
                  int playerId = ch - 'A';
                  if (!players.add(playerId))
                  {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("duplicate players detected in the map");
                  }
    
                  Player player = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlayer();
                  player.setId(playerId);
                  entityMap.put(position, player);
                }
                else if (ch >= 'a' && ch <= 'z')
                {
                  int playerId = Character.toUpperCase(ch) - 'A';
                  referencedPlayers.add(playerId);
                  boxCount++;
    
                  Box box = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createBox();
                  box.setPlayerId(playerId);
                  entityMap.put(position, box);
                }
                break;
            }
          }
        }
    
        if (players.isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("no player");
        }
    
        if (destinations.size() != boxCount)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("mismatch destinations");
        }
    
        if (!referencedPlayers.equals(players))
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("unmatched players");
        }
    
        GameMap gameMap = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameMap();
        gameMap.setMaxWidth(maxWidth);
        gameMap.setMaxHeight(maxHeight);
        gameMap.setUndoLimit(undoLimit);
        gameMap.getDestinations().addAll(destinations);
        gameMap.setMap(entityMap);

          }
        }

            position.setY(y);

                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createWall());
                break;
              case '.':
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
                break;
              case '@':
                destinations.add(position);
                entityMap.put(position, Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createEmpty());
                break;

                  }

                  entityMap.put(position, player);

                  referencedPlayers.add(playerId);
                  boxCount++;

                  box.setPlayerId(playerId);
                  entityMap.put(position, box);
                }
                break;
            }
          }
        }
    
        if (players.isEmpty())
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("no player");
        }
    
        if (destinations.size() != boxCount)
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("mismatch destinations");
        }
    
        if (!referencedPlayers.equals(players))
        {
          throw new IllegalArgumentException("unmatched players");
        }
    
        GameMap gameMap = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createGameMap();
        gameMap.setMaxWidth(maxWidth);
        gameMap.setMaxHeight(maxHeight);
        gameMap.setUndoLimit(undoLimit);
        gameMap.getDestinations().addAll(destinations);
        gameMap.setMap(entityMap);
        return gameMap;
